I'm not sure about iceberg lettuce, we have never grown it. When it comes to cauliflower and any members of the cabbage family, we have found several things to be helpful. The worst pests we have are slugs, which attack the new plant's leaves, and cabbage maggots, which attack the roots. The cabbage maggot insect lays eggs in the soil near the base of the plants. Dipel, which contains baccillus thuringensis, attacks the maggots. It is a great product. You mix it with water and pour it on the ground around the young plants. Diatomaceous earth lacerates the maggot's skin and causes it to bleed out, so it is a very satisfying product to use on the little bastards. We spread this on the ground when we transplant the starts. Then we put an 8" diameter ring of filter fabric on the ground over this. It is split to go around the plant start, with a very small hole in the middle. These are re-usable year after year. They cause the parent insect to lay eggs further away from the plant than it would like, and cause the maggots to have to crawl through a minefield of Dipel and D.E. The slugs are most harmful to the very young plants. An ambitious slug or two can kill a plant over night when it is small. Once the plants get bigger, slugs are much less of a problem. Slugs don't like to crawl across copper. We make spirals of junk copper wire or tubing by wrapping them around a soup can. They are roughly 3" diameter by 3" tall. We place these on top of the filter fabric and around the plant stem. They hold the leaves up off the ground. Slugs won't climb the copper, and are unable to jump high enough to reach the leaves. The copper ring stays around the base of the plant until it is harvested, then gets stored with the fabric rings and re-used the next season. I am not sure how you would use any of these methods if you plant directly instead of transplanting starts, but this is what works for us. Good luck!

In my area, cauliflower is plagued mainly by 3 pests. I tend to follow organic and natural practices in my food garden, and here are my options for brassicas.

  1. slugs: these are mainly a problem at the seedling stage, when they can kill the plant. I spray BT around the seedlings (once a week at the seedling stage). I also sprinkle liberally with Diatomaceous Earth. Both of these defenses will gradually weaken over time, so I get occasional slug damage but it is otherwise quite effective.
  2. aphids: I try to inspect the plants daily. My garden isn't huge, so it is really just walking around with my morning cup of coffee. When I see aphids, I hose them off with a spray of water. They tend to hide in the narrow spaces at the base of the leaves, so it takes a few seconds to make sure I got most of them. As a last resort for heavy infestations, I apply neem-oil spray (a few drops of neem oil in a soap solution). Neem is a little too effective because it also repels ladybugs (a natural aphid predator) and parasitoid wasps.
  3. caterpillars: Ever seen those pretty white butterflies around your garden? Those bastards lay eggs on your brassicas and their larvae eat cabbage leaves. There are also a few moths that like to lay eggs on brassica. I interplant brassicas with alliums (garlic, onion, chive). I only spray with BT if I see caterpillar damage in the vicinity. I avoid neem oil spray because it can deter parasitic flies and parasitic wasps.

(edit: This year, I plan to use the citrus-oil spray that TheBuddha wrote about. Seems like an attractive option.)
